name: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731
description:
Here is how to read the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 config.json. The architecture class is DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 4,096: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 129,280 × 4,096: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 64, so each head sees 512 dimensions (4,096 / 64). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 4096 / 64 = 512. 512 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 1, so this is multi-query attention (MQA): every query head shares a single key/value.

num_hidden_layers is 43: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

max_position_embeddings is 1,048,576 tokens — the context window in the config. rope_scaling is type yarn with factor 16, which stretches the rotary positions so the advertised window can be larger than the span the model originally trained on. rope_theta is 10000: that is the wavelength of the rotary embedding. A larger theta keeps distant tokens from aliasing after a full rotation.

vocab_size is 129,280. 129,280 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

This is a mixture of experts: 256 routed experts with top-k 6. The 1991 Jacobs / Jordan / Nowlan / Hinton paper “Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts” is the ancestor of this router-plus-specialists idea.

tie_word_embeddings is false, so the input embedding matrix and the output LM head are separate learned matrices rather than a shared transpose.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/blob/main/config.json.
